open_points.subject: A17 configuration and credential path traversal
open_points.text: the path is opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any of them, each component with Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW`
open_points.question: How are `.` and `..` components, repeated separators, and a trailing separator in an absolute configured path handled: literally, normalized before opening, or refused?
options: Refuse paths containing non-ordinary components
Normalize them before component-wise opening
Open every component literally
open_points.default_guess: Refuse `.` and `..`, collapse repeated separators, and refuse a trailing separator for the required regular file.

open_points.subject: A17 use of O_NOFOLLOW
open_points.text: each component with Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW`, whose presence no code tests (A20 rule 3)
open_points.question: Which other flags and component types are permitted when opening intermediate components, and what happens when the host or filesystem rejects `O_NOFOLLOW`?
options: Require intermediate components to be directories and treat any flag failure as the enclosing start or credential-resolution failure
Use `O_PATH` for intermediate components and a readable descriptor for the final file
Leave the exact open strategy platform-dependent
open_points.default_guess: Open each intermediate component relative to its parent as a directory with `O_NOFOLLOW`, open the final component as a readable regular file with `O_NOFOLLOW`, and map any failure to start refusal for configuration or `credential_unresolved` for a secret.

open_points.subject: A18 data-directory provisioning
open_points.text: At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory
open_points.question: Must the data directory, database, value area, fixture area and spool already exist, or does the kernel create any missing part, and with what behavior for a partially existing layout?
options: Create the directory and missing layout securely
Require the complete layout to exist
Create only an empty installation and refuse partial layouts
open_points.default_guess: Create a missing data directory and missing managed substructure with private permissions, but refuse incompatible existing objects.

open_points.subject: A18 private data-directory condition
open_points.text: The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
open_points.question: What exact ownership, permission bits, ACLs, special-file types and hard-link conditions satisfy “private,” and are they checked only at startup or again on use?
options: Require ownership by the effective kernel user and no group/other permission bits on every managed object
Require only that access-control evaluation denies other users
Apply different exact modes by object type
open_points.default_guess: Require the effective kernel user to own every managed object, require directories to have no group/other permissions and regular files to have no group/other permissions, refuse unexpected object types, and recheck an object when opened.

open_points.subject: A18 data-directory path and lock identity
open_points.text: a second process on the same directory refuses to start
open_points.question: What counts as the same directory when configured paths use symbolic links, bind mounts, different textual paths or filesystem aliases, and is the data-directory path itself allowed to be a symbolic link?
options: Identity is the opened directory inode and the path itself must be symlink-free
Identity is the canonical path
Only identical configured path strings conflict
open_points.default_guess: Open the directory without following symlinks, identify it by the opened filesystem object, and place the exclusive lock within that object so aliases contend on the same lock where the filesystem supports it.

open_points.subject: A18 startup checks
open_points.text: At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory; a second process on the same directory refuses to start. The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise. ... a link found at start stops the start
open_points.question: In what exact order are the lock, directory ownership and permission checks, symlink scan, database validation, cleanup, A17 configuration checks and A03 sandbox probe performed, and which failure is reported when several fail?
options: Specify one global startup-check order
Use the numbered decision order and define cross-decision precedence
Allow any detected startup failure to be reported
open_points.default_guess: Validate and securely open the configuration and data-directory path, acquire the lock, validate the managed layout, perform cleanup, validate the database, then run the sandbox probe before recovery and opening the surface.

open_points.subject: A18 transaction boundaries
open_points.text: Every change is one call to the store module and one transaction inside it
open_points.question: Which records and file publications constitute one “change” for each multi-record action, and therefore must commit atomically—for example run creation, admission plus activation, refusal plus run termination, and a node outcome plus produced values?
options: Each action names an explicit atomic store call
Each individual record mutation is a separate change
The store implementation may group mutations as convenient
open_points.default_guess: Treat every set of facts that another rule says is written together, and every externally visible state transition that would otherwise expose an impossible intermediate state, as one store call and transaction.

open_points.subject: A18 database and file crash consistency
open_points.text: Value bytes and spooled files are written to a temporary file, flushed, checked against their digest and size, and then renamed into place; a completed file a record names is never overwritten
open_points.question: What ordering and durability operations guarantee that a committed database record never names a missing, incomplete or uncommitted file after a crash?
options: Publish and durably sync the file and containing directory before committing its database reference
Commit the database first and repair missing files during recovery
Provide only process-failure atomicity, not power-loss durability
open_points.default_guess: Publish and fsync the file and its containing directory before committing the SQLite transaction that names it, with SQLite configured for durable commit; an earlier crash may leave only an unreferenced complete file.

open_points.subject: A18 later filesystem mutation
open_points.text: a link found later makes that store call fail with nothing written
open_points.question: What happens when a managed object encountered later is missing, has changed owner or permissions, is the wrong non-symlink type, has unexpected hard links, or its recorded bytes fail digest or size checks?
options: Fail the store call like a later symlink and write nothing
Stop the kernel immediately
Attempt to recreate or repair the object
open_points.default_guess: Fail the call with `internal_error`, expose no bytes, commit no records, and stop after answering as A14 rule 7 requires.

open_points.subject: A18 failed-call filesystem residue
open_points.text: a link found later makes that store call fail with nothing written
open_points.question: Does “nothing written” prohibit even a published but unreferenced file, or does A18 rule 3's allowance that a failed call may leave “a published file no record names” also apply when the failure is a later symlink?
options: Symlink detection must occur before any publication, leaving no filesystem change
An unreferenced published file is allowed but no record may commit
“Nothing written” means only no database record
open_points.default_guess: Preflight all paths for the call before publication; if a race is detected later, permit only a complete unreferenced file and never a committed record.

open_points.subject: A18 startup cleanup failures
open_points.text: On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... and the spool directories of runs that ended and do not keep their spool ... are removed; nothing else is. A spool directory that cannot be removed does not stop the start
open_points.question: Does failure to enumerate or remove a temporary file or unreferenced value stop startup, as opposed to the explicitly tolerated failure to remove an obsolete spool directory?
options: Only obsolete spool-directory removal failures are tolerated
All cleanup failures are tolerated and affected objects are never served
Any cleanup failure stops startup
open_points.default_guess: Stop startup if the kernel cannot enumerate the managed areas or remove temporary and unreferenced value files; tolerate only the explicitly named obsolete spool-directory removal failure.

open_points.subject: A18 corrupted or incomplete store
open_points.text: The data directory holds one SQLite database with every kernel record, a content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures named by digest, and the run spool
open_points.question: What must startup do when the SQLite database is malformed or inconsistent, or a record names a missing, truncated or digest-mismatched durable value or trial fixture?
options: Refuse to start and report store corruption
Start but fail only requests that reach damaged data
Delete or reconstruct damaged records or files
open_points.default_guess: Refuse to start without editing or deleting the damaged records or named durable files.

open_points.subject: A18 request serialization order
open_points.text: Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive
open_points.question: What observable event defines arrival order when concurrent MCP requests are received: complete message receipt, transport acceptance, authentication completion, or insertion into an explicit sequence?
options: Assign a sequence when the complete bounded request message is received
Assign a sequence when the connection or stream is accepted
Permit the transport scheduler to choose among concurrent requests
open_points.default_guess: Assign a monotonically increasing sequence when a complete request message has been received, before validation, and process requests by that sequence.

open_points.subject: A20 supported Linux platform
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named
open_points.question: Which Linux kernel capabilities or minimum version, CPU architectures, userspace ABI and libc environments are supported, and is an otherwise unsupported Linux host rejected by a check or merely outside the release guarantee?
options: Name a fixed support matrix
Define support by required capabilities and startup probes
Claim support for every Linux version and architecture
open_points.default_guess: Define support by a documented set of required Linux capabilities plus supported CPU and userspace targets, and refuse startup when a safely testable required capability is absent.

open_points.subject: A20 filesystem prerequisites for A18 guarantees
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named
open_points.question: Does every Linux filesystem qualify even when it cannot provide the exclusive locking, atomic rename, directory durability or SQLite locking semantics A18 requires, or must the release restrict or probe the data-directory filesystem?
options: Restrict the data directory to explicitly supported local filesystems
Probe required filesystem semantics at startup
Treat A18 guarantees as applying to every Linux filesystem without detection
open_points.default_guess: Require a local filesystem that provides SQLite-supported locking, atomic same-directory rename and durable fsync semantics, and refuse known unsupported filesystem types.
